title: Simultaneous K-flat word models and normalized comparison descent
statement:
Let a finite collection of small sites $\mathcal C_i$ with sheaves of commutative rings $R_i$ be given, in fixed sufficiently large universes [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Put $\mathcal A_i=\operatorname{Mod}(R_i)$ and let $Q_i$ denote localization of their unbounded cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Each edge $a:i\to j$ is the ordinary additive pullback $F_a:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$ of a specified morphism of ringed topoi, including extension of scalars on the identity underlying topos. Choose its total left derived functor $LF_a$ with universal cochain counit $\varepsilon_a:LF_aQ_i\to Q_jC(F_a)$, normalized to the canonical K-flat computation of ringed pullback; an exact $F_a$ may instead use its canonically identified exact derived functor. Here $C(F_a)$ means degreewise application. A word $w=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ is a finite composable string, with $F_w=F_{a_r}\cdots F_{a_1}$, $LF_w=LF_{a_r}\cdots LF_{a_1}$; the empty word is the identity. Let $\varepsilon_w:LF_wQ_i\to Q_jC(F_w)$ be the composite of the edge counits in this order.

Every complex $K$ admits one quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to K$ of entire $R_i$-module complexes, with $P$ K-flat and all its terms flat [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For this same $P$, every intermediate $C(F_{a_s}\cdots F_{a_1})P$ in every finite word starting at $i$ is K-flat with flat terms, and every $\varepsilon_{w,P}$ is invertible. For words $w,v:i\to j$ and an ordinary natural transformation $t:F_w\to F_v$, there is a unique natural transformation $t^L:LF_w\to LF_v$ with
$$\varepsilon_{v,P}\circ t^L_{Q_iP}=Q_j(C(t)_P)\circ\varepsilon_{w,P}$$
for every flat-term K-flat $P$. This assignment preserves identities, vertical composition and whiskering by any of the specified edge functors, using the displayed composite counits for words; it takes ordinary isomorphisms to derived isomorphisms. Consequently every equality of finite pastings of such ordinary transformations induces the corresponding equality of the normalized derived transformations. Natural transformations between the derived word functors are determined on these $Q_iP$.

In particular the derived scalar associator for $R\to S\to T$ is uniquely normalized by the ordinary map $c\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto cb\otimes x$, and identity scalar change is uniquely identified with the identity by $s\otimes x\mapsto sx$. The result applies when each $\mathcal C_i$ is a ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]: $P$ resolves the whole strict system, and the formulas are identities there before any evaluation or inverse limit. No boundedness, normalization, finite Tor-amplitude or flatness of any structural ring map is assumed.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_i$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes on the ith ringed site. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], choose a single quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to K$ with $P\in\mathcal P_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], each specified edge sends $\mathcal P_i$ into $\mathcal P_j$, including scalar change on the identity topos, without requiring the structural ring map to be flat. Induct on the length of a word: length zero leaves $P$ unchanged; adjoining the next edge preserves membership in the next $\mathcal P$. Thus this same $P$ works for all words, independently of how many words are considered. The resolution theorem records flatness using the monoidal tensor presentation; transport exactness through siteSheafTensorRightIso [def-pur-site-sheaf-tensor-presentation-data] to obtain the stated IsFlatOnSite predicate.

By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-resolving-computation], the specified universal edge counit $\varepsilon_{a,P}$ is invertible for $P\in\mathcal P_i$. This applies to the actual chosen left-derived pair, not just to an abstract isomorphic functor; the exact alternative has the canonical identification required in the statement. For a word $w:i\to j$ and an edge $a:j\to k$, the definition of the composite counit is
$$\varepsilon_{aw,P}=\varepsilon_{a,C(F_w)P}\circ LF_a(\varepsilon_{w,P}).$$
For the empty word the counit is the identity. Step 1 makes $C(F_w)P$ resolving; induction and preservation of isomorphisms by a functor show that every displayed composite is invertible.

For $t:F_w\to F_v$ and $P\in\mathcal P_i$, put
$$\alpha_P=\varepsilon_{v,P}^{-1}\circ Q_j(C(t)_P)\circ\varepsilon_{w,P}.$$
Naturality of the two counits and of $C(t)$ gives $LF_v(Q_i f)\circ\alpha_P=\alpha_{P'}\circ LF_w(Q_i f)$ for every chain map $f:P\to P'$ in $\mathcal P_i$: substitute the formula and cancel the two counit isomorphisms. Work now in the homotopy category of complexes, whose localization is the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An additive functor sends a homotopy $f-g=dh+hd$ to $F(f)-F(g)=dF(h)+F(h)d$, so the above equality holds for every homotopy class as well. The objects of the homotopy category are the complexes themselves; hence this supplies exactly a natural family on its full subcategory $\mathcal P_i$.

Apply [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class] with source the homotopy category, weak equivalences its quasi-isomorphisms, resolving predicate $\mathcal P_i$, and functors $A=LF_wQ_i$, $B=LF_vQ_i$ valued in $D(\mathcal A_j)$. The right calculus of fractions is [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]; the incoming resolutions are those of Step 1, and $A$ inverts all quasi-isomorphisms because $Q_i$ does. Step 3 verifies the required naturality on every morphism between resolving objects. We obtain a natural transformation $\beta:LF_wQ_i\to LF_vQ_i$. Both these functors factor through the localization of the homotopy category, so the full faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], clause (2), gives a natural transformation $t^L:LF_w\to LF_v$ whose restriction is $\beta$. Its components on resolving objects are $\alpha_P$, giving the required normalization.

proof.text:
If $\sigma,\tau:LF_w\to LF_v$ agree on the $Q_iP$, naturality along the resolution $p:P\to K$ gives, for either transformation,
$$\sigma_{Q_iK}=LF_v(Q_i p)\circ\sigma_{Q_iP}\circ LF_w(Q_i p)^{-1}.$$
Thus their components agree on every $Q_iK$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes them equal. The same argument works for any two functors out of $D(\mathcal A_i)$, proving the final determination assertion and uniqueness of the normalization in Step 4.

For an identity $t$, the formula of Step 3 is an identity. For $t:F_w\to F_v$ and $s:F_v\to F_u$, multiplication of the two formulas cancels $\varepsilon_{v,P}\varepsilon_{v,P}^{-1}$ and gives $\alpha_{s,P}\alpha_{t,P}=\alpha_{st,P}$. Step 5 then gives preservation of identity and vertical composition. If $t$ is an ordinary isomorphism, apply this to its ordinary inverse; the two descended composites are identities, so $t^L$ is an isomorphism.

Check precomposition by an edge $b:h\to i$. Write $B=C(F_b)P$ for $P\in\mathcal P_h$, so $B\in\mathcal P_i$ by Step 1. Naturality of $t^L$ along the isomorphism $\varepsilon_{b,P}:LF_bQ_hP\to Q_iB$ gives
$$LF_v(\varepsilon_{b,P})\circ t^L_{LF_bQ_hP}=t^L_{Q_iB}\circ LF_w(\varepsilon_{b,P}).$$
Postcompose with $\varepsilon_{v,B}$ and apply the normalization at $B$. Using $\varepsilon_{vb,P}=\varepsilon_{v,B}\circ LF_v(\varepsilon_{b,P})$ and the analogous formula for $w$, the result is
$$\varepsilon_{vb,P}\circ t^L_{LF_bQ_hP}=Q_j(C(t)_{B})\circ\varepsilon_{wb,P}.$$
This is precisely the required normalization for the ordinary cell $tF_b$. Step 5 identifies its descent with the prewhiskered $t^L$.

For postcomposition by $a:j\to k$, naturality of the edge counit on the chain map $C(t)_P:C(F_w)P\to C(F_v)P$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{a,C(F_v)P}\circ LF_a(Q_j(C(t)_P))=Q_k(C(F_a)C(t)_P)\circ\varepsilon_{a,C(F_w)P}.$$
Apply $LF_a$ to the normalization for $t$, and substitute this equality and the composite counit formulas. This gives
$$\varepsilon_{av,P}\circ LF_a(t^L_{Q_iP})=Q_k(C(F_at)_P)\circ\varepsilon_{aw,P}.$$
By Step 5 this is the descent of $F_at$. Steps 7 and 8 iterate over arbitrary words. Every finite pasting is built from these two whiskerings, vertical composition and identities; substitute the proved compatibilities at each operation. Equal ordinary pastings therefore have the same descended transformation. No assertion that a nonexact edge preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms was used.

For scalar extension along a and b, use [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] to equip the three prescribed ordinary functors with extension/restriction adjunctions whose units send x to the sheafified 1 tensor x. Successive restrictions equal restriction along a composite by the canonical isomorphism having identity section maps. Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq gives Fa.E followed by Fb.E isomorphic to Fba.E. Transpose its component twice. The adjoint uniqueness equation identifies the double transpose with the unit of Fba. Linearity and the normalized units give t tensor (s tensor x) mapping to (b(s) * t) tensor x. Identity restriction is similarly the identity by its canonical sectionwise identity; left adjoint uniqueness gives F.E isomorphic to the identity, and its transpose equation gives s tensor x mapping to s*x. Apply the generic resolving-class descent argument of Steps 3-5 to the cochain comparison maps. The source comparison is the composite of Fa and Fb counits. Its components are invertible on resolving complexes, since Fa computes on K-flat complexes and [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings-all-independent] makes Fa(P) K-flat, so Fb computes there too. The target counit is invertible by Fba.computes. Descending an ordinary isomorphism yields an isomorphism: its resolving components are invertible; naturality along incoming quasi-isomorphisms propagates this to every Q(K), and essential surjectivity of Q propagates it to every derived object. The identity scalar comparison is the same construction with target counit the identity. Uniqueness is the uniqueness already proved in Step 5. This argument permits independent universes for all three chosen derived categories.

proof.text: By [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], a strict quotient-semilinear system is a module sheaf on the single sequence ringed site. Apply Step 1 there, taking $K$ to be its entire complex. The augmentation $P\to K$ is one morphism of module-sheaf complexes on that site, and every $C(F_w)P$, counit and $C(t)_P$ above is formed there. Hence the normalization and the pasting equations already hold in its unbounded derived category; the ordinary formulas used to produce them are morphisms of the entire strict systems. This construction makes no evaluation or inverse-limit operation. The arguments used only flat-term K-flat replacement and ringed pullback preservation, which impose none of the additional boundedness, normalization, Tor-amplitude or structural-flatness assumptions listed in the statement.
